analysis.title: The BEAT: Quarterly Global Market and Asset Allocation Guide, Q4 2026 - October
key_insights: Portfolio Solutions Group (PSG) moves to overweight global equities vs fixed income, citing stronger nominal growth, AI productivity gains and strong corporate earnings. Headline view: 'Rates Are Up. Growth Is Strong. Stay Constructive.'

Yields are rising mainly because nominal growth is strong. Central banks are removing accommodation, not imposing restraint. Geopolitical, energy and inflation risks could turn 'good' yield increases into bad ones, but the balance is constructive for now.

Duration: slightly underweight. UST 10-year yields are back near 5% after the collapse of the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) and a rebound in oil, the highest since late 2023. Nominal GDP growth is well above policy rates.

Corporate credit: spreads are near all-time tights, so risk/reward is poor. PSG is underweight investment grade, neutral high yield, and prefers MBS/ABS and bank loans. ABS/MBS is the highest-conviction fixed income overweight.

US equities overweight: growth resilience, earnings strength, fiscal stimulus from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, deregulation and AI adoption. The US is more insulated from energy disruption than the rest of the world.
US SMID (small/mid-cap) overweight vs large-cap, on broadening growth and an industrial recovery. Cyclicals are overweight vs defensives on policy-driven structural tailwinds.

Europe underweight: the Iran war's energy price effect, low gas storage into winter and weak EPS growth. Preferences within Europe are banks, utilities and grid equipment providers. Eurozone bonds are underweight duration, with overweight Spain/Portugal vs France/Germany.
Japan is neutral overall but overweight Japanese banks, with conviction upgraded. The forward market is pricing a 2% BoJ policy rate, supporting re-rating and ROE gains.

Emerging markets equities neutral. AI beneficiaries Taiwan and Korea lead earnings revisions. China has weak domestic momentum. India is underweight: forward P/E premium near 100% vs EM, no AI exposure and energy headwinds.

EM hard currency debt cut to neutral because spreads are near all-time tights and fundamentals have weakened. EM local currency stays overweight via Brazil (rates above 13%, inflation about 4%, central bank expected to keep cutting).
Municipal bonds moved tactically overweight as muni/UST ratios returned to the high end of their multi-year range. TIPS remain overweight on rising breakevens after the MOU collapse.

Commodities neutral. The Iran war lifted energy and any resolution would likely reverse it sharply. Refined products (diesel) are the main stress point. Industrial metals are at risk if energy disrupts the cycle. Precious metals face headwinds from the Fed's hawkish shift and a stronger USD.

Macro backdrop: growth resilient/accelerating, inflation sticky without wage spillover, labor market firming but not overheating, gradual Fed tightening toward neutral, expansionary fiscal. Key risk: an oil supply shock forcing central banks to overtighten.

Core PCE has surged to 3.3%, contributing to the Fed's hawkish shift, but trimmed mean inflation shows disinflationary pressure. Inflation is concentrated in select categories such as AI- and tariff-related. Citi inflation surprise index shows prints in line or slightly better than consensus.
Forwards price rate hikes from all four major central banks (Fed, ECB, BoJ, BoE) by mid-2027, driven by the energy shock and supply constraints rather than demand.

Nominal GDP growth is near 6%, almost 3 points above the policy rate, so PSG argues the Fed has room to hike before restraining growth. Recessions have historically followed the Fed pushing rates above nominal growth.
The 10-year term premium has been broadly flat over the past year in the US and Germany (higher in Japan), so PSG reads higher long rates as a shifting Fed outlook rather than fiscal stress.

Equity gains in 2026 have come from earnings, not multiples. MSCI ACWI 12-month forward EPS is up 30% YTD while forward P/E is down 14%. Growth/Tech revisions are about +29% for CY2026 and +19% for CY2027, and upward revisions are spreading into cyclicals.

AI demand: OpenRouter token demand reached 113 trillion per week at end of August, up 25x YoY and 2x MoM. Nvidia revenue guidance implies 70% growth for fiscal 2028 vs consensus 45%. AI and tech exports are about 70% of Asia's export growth.
Cyclicals have underperformed defensives since July after the US-Iran MOU unraveled. The open question is whether economic data deteriorates or the cyclical trade rebounds.
EM semiconductor forward P/E premium has fully unwound to roughly in line with the rest of EM even as earnings keep rising.

Oil: crude is rangebound since the Iran war began, inventories are declining, and the main risk sits in refined products because of lost refining capacity. Europe's relative economic performance tracks energy prices.

Alternatives: private equity neutral to positive (AI is about 70% of VC deal value, buyout distributions soft). Private credit neutral, prefer loss avoidance and special situations, with direct lending concerns receding. Infrastructure neutral to positive (AI power demand vs financing and permitting constraints). Real estate neutral to positive. Natural resources neutral and the weakest complex.

Market monitor at 9/30/26: 10-year Treasury 5.27%, 30-year 5.62%, 2-year 4.87%. US Agg returned -3.51% over 3 months and 1.84% negative over 1 year. US HY spread 312 bps and loans 481 bps. S&P 500 YTD +12.75%, MSCI EM YTD +23.38%, Nikkei YTD +33.35%, S&P Info Tech YTD +28.38%, S&P Energy YTD +40.28%.
Commodities: Bloomberg Commodity Index +32.87% YTD, Brent +110.17% YTD, heating oil +184.69% YTD, gold -4.45% YTD, silver -14.74% YTD. In September gold fell 6.28% and silver 9.30%.

earnings_insights: Nvidia revenue guidance for fiscal year 2028 came in at 70% growth, vs consensus expectation of 45% growth (guidance vs consensus estimate, as of 9/1/2026).

Expected S&P 500 EPS growth and 2025 EPS growth figures are given by region and sector in the FactSet charts (as of 9/30/26). Expected energy EPS growth shows about 95.9% and communications about 56.1%, info tech about 52.6%, per the chart data.
India's forward EPS growth expectations look subpar vs EM, while its forward P/E premium is close to 100%.

risk_factors: Oil supply shock forces central banks to overtighten, turning growth-driven yield increases into demand destruction.
Uncontained inflation would require central banks to move from removing accommodation to actively destroying demand.
Energy and refined products (diesel) disruption from the Iran war.
Tight credit spreads leave little margin of safety, especially in HY and EM hard currency.
Higher US rates complicate EM debt selection.
Cyclical sectors could deteriorate if energy prices disrupt the economic cycle.
Hawkish Fed shift and USD appreciation as headwinds for precious metals.
Europe's low gas storage heading into winter.
Late-stage AI valuations and concentration in venture capital, and sustainability of AI-driven earnings.
charts_described: Chart on p.15 plots US Fed funds vs US nominal growth, with nominal growth nearly 3% above the policy rate and past recessions marked when the Fed over-tightened.
Chart on p.22 shows US core PCE at 3.3% alongside trimmed mean inflation, which indicates disinflationary pressure persisting.
Chart on p.23 shows forwards pricing rate hikes from the Fed, ECB, BoJ and BoE by mid-2027.
Chart on p.26 shows AI/tech exports as roughly 70% of Asia's export growth.
Chart on p.39 shows OpenRouter weekly token demand reaching 113 trillion per week at end of August.
Chart on p.33 shows US IG option-adjusted spread near historical tights relative to MBS.
vol_and_positioning: Fund flows (8/31/26): Large Blend ETFs took in $30,910M in a month and Large Blend mutual funds saw $27,661M of outflows. Technology ETFs had $2,066M of outflows in the month but $31,468M of inflows over three months.
Intermediate Core Bond mutual funds saw the largest monthly bond inflows at $7,355M. Derivative Income ETFs drew $6,025M in a month.
Trailing P/E, NTM P/E and VIX charts are included in the market monitor but the text gives no VIX level.
Corporate credit spreads: US IG at 80 bps, HY at 312 bps, loans 481 bps, with annual HY default rate 2.04% (vs 0.49% 12 months ago).
geopolitical: Iran war and the collapse of the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) drove a rebound in oil prices and higher yields.
Energy is described as the geopolitical fault line, with tight refined-product markets, particularly diesel, transmitting disruption into inflation.
Europe has unusually low gas storage entering winter and remains vulnerable to elevated energy prices.
Efforts to stabilize the yen and a resilient US dollar help contain global volatility.
China's manufacturing export resurgence ('China Shock 2.0') is widening its trade surplus and adding competitive pressure on global producers.
France has political uncertainty compounding its fiscal problems.

tension_points.bull_case: Yields rise on strong nominal growth (near 6%) well above policy rates, supporting earnings, cash flows and credit, so risk assets can keep rising.
tension_points.bear_case: Geopolitical, energy and inflation risks can turn good yield increases into bad ones, and an oil shock could force central banks to overtighten.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation becoming uncontained, so central banks must move to actively destroying demand.

tension_points.bull_case: Economic data remains supportive, with global PMIs accelerating, so the cyclical trade can rebound.
tension_points.bear_case: Cyclicals have underperformed defensives since July after the MOU unraveled, which may signal deteriorating economic data.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deterioration in the global manufacturing PMI while cyclicals keep lagging defensives.
